Track B — NT LLR vs conservation score on TraitGym

children.label: Track B — NT LLR vs conservation score on TraitGym

children.value: (3,380 variants, 338 positives, 9 matched controls per 1 positive = 338

s, 19 chromosomes). The metric is AUPRC. The sign of each score was fixed before looking at the data (LLR −, conservation +). Δ = AUPRC(model) − AUPRC(baseline). The decision rule is ‘supported’ if all three of the following conditions hold: the mean of the per-chromosome Δ (the 14 chromosomes with ≥ 5 positives) is 0.02 or more; the number of chromosomes with Δ > 0 is 10/14 or more; and the lower bound of the 95% interval of the
-level paired bootstrap (500 resamples) is greater than 0. The per-score permutation null has 1,000 resamples.

: The score files and the variant table have the same number of rows, there is no NaN, each group has exactly 1 positive, each group lies within one chromosome, and there are no duplicate variants. All of them passed.
, a comparison against the pooled-AUPRC distribution of 1,000 shuffles of that score’s own values within
. The null mean is 0.100–0.102, the 95% quantile is 0.103–0.112, and the minimum of p is 0.001.
NT LLR − phyloP-241m: pooled Δ −0.571 [−0.618, −0.519], chromosome-mean Δ −0.561, 0/14 chromosomes with Δ > 0, so it is
The secondary comparison Evo2-7B LLR − phyloP-241m has Δ −0.293 [−0.348, −0.231], 1/14, and is not supported. Both comparisons were pre-specified, and no multiple-comparison correction was made.
: The negative control shuffles the model score within

, and its AUPRC is 0.096 (the null mean of NT LLR is 0.102). The positive control is Evo2-7B LLR vs TSS distance only, with pooled Δ +0.266 [+0.213, +0.314], chromosome-mean Δ +0.231, 13/14, so it is ‘supported’.

: Changing the baseline to phyloP-100v and to phastCons-43p is still not supported in both cases (Δ −0.550 / −0.394). Changing the minimum number of positives per chromosome to 3 and to 10 gives Δ > 0 in only 1 of 17 and 0 of 10 chromosomes, respectively.

It matches the AUPRC of module 03 notebook 02 (NT 0.103, Evo2-7B 0.38, phyloP-241m 0.67, TSS 0.115). The permutation p did not match before the cross-review of this record. Notebook 02 used a single null distribution for all scores (the values obtained by shuffling the within-group ranks 0…9), giving NT 0.34 and TSS 0.006. The permutation distribution of the observed statistic (pooled AUPRC) is obtained by shuffling each score’s own values, so notebook 02 was fixed in the same way (see “Cross-review” below), and it is now NT 0.41 (this script gives 0.445 because the seed is different; Monte Carlo standard error about 0.015) and TSS 0.001.

Track D — Cutoff sweep of the Lipophilicity cluster split (module 05 exercise 1)

children.label: Track D — Cutoff sweep of the Lipophilicity cluster split (module 05 exercise 1)

children.value: : 4,200 Lipophilicity molecules (0 invalid SMILES, 0 duplicates), ECFP4 count (2048) vs ChemBERTa-77M-MLM mean-pooled last layer (revision pinned), a RidgeCV linear head, 5-fold × 5 repeats, the cutoffs {0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6} and a random split. The metric is RMSE, and Δ = RMSE(ECFP4) − RMSE(MLM) (positive = MLM is better). The bootstrap is done 300 times in units of Butina clusters. The decision rule is: mean of the per-repeat Δ ≥ 0.02, repeats with Δ > 0 ≥ 4/5, and interval lower bound > 0.
(test→train nearest Tanimoto of the first repeat):
Fraction of test molecules that still have a neighbor at or above the cutoff in train

As the cutoff is raised, the clusters split more finely and the nearest similarity goes up. Because the clusters are not transitive, pairs at or above the cutoff remain across folds (74% of the test set at 0.3).
(negative control) RMSE of ECFP4 trained on shuffled labels, compared with the
The standard deviation of y is 1.203, and when the labels are shuffled the value should converge to this, and it did.

The intervals include 0 at 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5, and the gap is not monotonic in the cutoff (smallest at 0.4 and larger again at 0.6). The control, the pretraining effect (MLM vs random initialization), has Δ +0.16 to +0.21 and 5/5 in all 5 splits, so it is ‘supported’.
Observation on the question of exercise 1

: The hypothesis that “raising the cutoff always makes it harder” did not hold in this setting. The ECFP4 RMSE mostly went down (it became easier), from 0.906 to 0.827, going from cutoff 0.3 to 0.6. The rise from 0.3 to 0.4 (0.012) is at the level of the repeat sd of 0.006–0.008. It is in the same range as the values in the module 05 README (random 0.750, about 0.923 near cluster 0.4; 3 repeats).
What was changed from the template

: Ridge and Spearman were replaced by RidgeCV and RMSE, and position blocks by Butina clusters. The random split has no cluster unit, so the bootstrap unit was arbitrarily set to the cutoff-0.4 clusters (the meaning of the interval is not exactly the same as in the other cells). The functions of notebook 05/01 are inside cells and cannot be imported, so the
, Butina and ChemBERTa pooling code was copied into the script.
: It is the result for Lipophilicity only, frozen embeddings + a linear head, and a fixed layer and pooling (last-layer mean). Other tasks, fine-tuning and MTR variants were not covered.

and the order “preregistration → provenance → inspection → controls → sensitivity” were used as they were. For comparisons without training, as in track B, the
The controls had to be redefined for each track.

The negative control was “shuffling scores within groups” in B, “shuffling the training labels” in C and “shuffling labels” in D, and the positive control that shows the decision rule can output ‘supported’ was “Evo2-7B vs TSS distance only” in B and “pretraining vs random initialization” in C and D. Without these positive controls we could not have told whether the “not supported” of the three tracks was a bias of the rule.
That all three primary comparisons came out “not supported” is partly because of the
of question (asking whether an FM beats a strong baseline). It is not a new conclusion, but in the same direction as modules 03, 04 and 05.
